diff --git a/llvm/test/Analysis/MemorySSA/call-loop-carried-dependency.ll b/llvm/test/Analysis/MemorySSA/call-loop-carried-dependency.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..c27de9f79814
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Analysis/MemorySSA/call-loop-carried-dependency.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --check-inst-comments --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='print<memoryssa-walker>' -disable-output < %s 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+
+; Make sure that the memcpy is clobbered by the memoryphi, not by liveOnEntry.
+define void @test(i1 %c, ptr %path, ptr %name) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @test(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[C:%.*]], ptr [[PATH:%.*]], ptr [[NAME:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP:%.*]] = alloca [260 x i8], align 16
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[WHILE_BODY:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[WHILE_BODY]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ; 3 = MemoryPhi({entry,liveOnEntry},{while.body,1})
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[IV_NEXT:%.*]], %[[WHILE_BODY]] ], [ 259, %[[ENTRY]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT]] = add nsw i64 [[IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_IV:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds [260 x i8], ptr [[TMP]], i64 0, i64 [[IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ; 1 = MemoryDef(3)->3 - clobbered by 3 = MemoryPhi({entry,liveOnEntry},{while.body,1})
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i8 42, ptr [[TMP_IV]], align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C]], label %[[WHILE_BODY]], label %[[EXIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_IV_1:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr [[TMP_IV]], i64 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SUB7:%.*]] = sub nsw i64 259, [[IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ; 2 = MemoryDef(1)->3 - clobbered by 3 = MemoryPhi({entry,liveOnEntry},{while.body,1})
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 1 [[NAME]], ptr nonnull align 1 [[TMP_IV_1]], i64 [[SUB7]], i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca [260 x i8], align 16
+  br label %while.body
+
+while.body:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.next, %while.body ], [ 259, %entry ]
+  %iv.next = add nsw i64 %iv, -1
+  %tmp.iv = getelementptr inbounds [260 x i8], ptr %tmp, i64 0, i64 %iv
+  store i8 42, ptr %tmp.iv, align 1
+  br i1 %c, label %while.body, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  %tmp.iv.1 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %tmp.iv, i64 1
+  %sub7 = sub nsw i64 259, %iv
+  call void @llvm.memcpy(ptr align 1 %name, ptr nonnull align 1 %tmp.iv.1, i64 %sub7, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

top_candidates.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: LICM's noConflictingReadWrites changes its MemorySSA access scan for hoisting: when the operation is not being sunk, it now skips a candidate MemoryAccess if the instruction's MemoryDef/MemoryUse representation (IMD) dominates that access according to MSSA->dominates. The commit also adds LICM coverage for inaccessible-memory calls and updates MemorySSA expected graphs, reflecting altered memory-access relationships or optimized IR in affected tests.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA::dominates; LICMPass; LNICMPass
Behavioral change: For a hoist operation, noConflictingReadWrites ignores an examined MemorySSA access when MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA) is true.; The skip is explicitly disabled for sinking via !Flags.getIsSink(), so the changed access-filtering rule applies only to the hoist path.; LICM may therefore classify some loop memory accesses as non-conflicting and permit hoisting that the prior scan would have rejected.; The added tests distinguish hoisting a write to inaccessible memory when no conflicting inaccessible-memory read exists from retaining it when a conflicting read exists.
Assertion or trace link: MSSA->dominates directly matches the issue's MSSA.dominates signal.; The change is in LICM code that explicitly receives and preserves MemorySSA.; The issue concerns MemorySSA clobber-walker verification and memory-dependence reasoning; this patch changes how LICM filters MemorySSA accesses during memory-conflict analysis.
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests exercise loop hoisting around calls with inaccessible-memory effects, not the reported reduced C testcase.; No visible test invokes ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult or reproduces an assertion failure.; Because LICM runs with loop-mssa and its changed hoisting decisions can alter MemorySSA accesses and their dominance relationships, it is a plausible route to expose a MemorySSA verification failure at optimization time.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; MemorySSA; MemorySSA dominance reasoning; loop-mssa
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate in the supplied evidence. It makes a substantive MemorySSA-dependent control-flow decision in LICM, directly calls MSSA->dominates, and changes the set of accesses considered conflicting for hoisting. Such a change can alter MemorySSA-backed optimization behavior and exercise clobber-walker verification differently. However, the visible hunks do not modify MemorySSA.cpp or ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult and do not show the reported assertion, so the link is plausible rather than proven.
Causal confidence: 0.68
Build risk: The implementation change is small but changes a correctness-sensitive LICM memory-safety predicate.; A new LICM regression test covers both positive and negative inaccessible-memory hoisting cases.; Existing MemorySSA analysis test expectations were updated, providing evidence that observable MemorySSA output changed.; The available test coverage does not show a direct verifier-assertion regression test for ClobberWalker.

behavioral_change: For a hoist operation, noConflictingReadWrites ignores an examined MemorySSA access when MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA) is true.

LICM may therefore classify some loop memory accesses as non-conflicting and permit hoisting that the prior scan would have rejected.
The added tests distinguish hoisting a write to inaccessible memory when no conflicting inaccessible-memory read exists from retaining it when a conflicting read exists.

Summary: This nominally NFC Scalar-transforms change narrows generic BranchInst uses to CondBrInst or UncondBrInst in loop idiom recognition, loop predication, induction-variable simplification, jump threading, and DFA jump threading. The visible logic continues to operate only on the appropriate branch form, including using an explicit UncondBrInst cast before DFA jump threading unfolds control flow and updates the dominator tree.
Changed symbols: detectPopcountIdiom; detectShiftUntilZeroIdiom; JumpThreadingPass::threadEdge; JumpThreadingPass::tryToUnfoldSelect; LoopPredication::predicateLoopExits; DFAJumpThreading::unfold; LoopIdiomRecognize::insertFFSIfProfitable; IndVarSimplify::optimizeLoopExits

evidence: Directly changes LICM's MemorySSA-based legality decision by adding MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA), matching the issue's MSSA.dominates signal.
Newly permitted hoists can alter MemorySSA update and clobber relationships, plausibly producing an OtherClobbers or ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult invariant failure at optimization time.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This LICM change refines noConflictingReadWrites for hoisting: while scanning MemorySSA accesses, a non-sinking transformation now skips an access when the instruction's MemoryDef/Use state IMD dominates that access according to MemorySSA. The patch changes LICM hoisting outcomes, adds inaccessible-memory call hoisting coverage, and updates MemorySSA print expectations for existing CFG cases.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA; LICMPass; LNICMPass
Behavioral change: For non-sinking LICM operations, noConflictingReadWrites ignores scanned MemorySSA accesses dominated by IMD via MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA).; Changes which accesses are considered conflicting during LICM hoist-safety analysis, potentially permitting additional hoists when only dominated accesses remain.; Exercises LICM with loop-mssa and changes expected MemorySSA def/phi structure in MemorySSA analysis tests.; Adds coverage that hoists a write to inaccessible memory when it does not conflict, while retaining a similar write in-loop when another inaccessible-memory reader can conflict.
Assertion or trace link: MSSA.dominates; MemorySSA
Reproducer link: MemorySSA-backed LICM loop-hoisting behavior; loop-mssa(licm) execution
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; MemorySSA; MemorySSA-backed scalar optimization
Causal explanation: This is a strong subsystem match: the issue implicates MemorySSA dominance and clobber-walker verification, while the changed LICM safety check directly calls MSSA->dominates and changes MemorySSA-driven transformation decisions. A newly permitted hoist can require corresponding MemorySSA updates, so an error in the altered dominance-based filtering could plausibly expose a later verifier failure. The retrieved hunks do not show ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult, OtherClobbers handling, the reported testcase, or a direct assertion, so the causal link is plausible but not proven.

Summary: This LICM change refines noConflictingReadWrites for hoisting: while scanning MemorySSA accesses, a non-sinking transformation now skips an access when the instruction's MemoryDef/Use state IMD dominates that access according to MemorySSA. The patch changes LICM hoisting outcomes, adds inaccessible-memory call hoisting coverage, and updates MemorySSA print expectations for existing CFG cases.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopTransformWarning/vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopTransformWarning/vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..0168bddacca5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopTransformWarning/vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='loop-vectorize,loop-unroll,transform-warning' \
+; RUN:   -force-vector-width=4 -force-vector-interleave=1 \
+; RUN:   -enable-epilogue-vectorization -epilogue-vectorization-force-VF=4 \
+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-missed=transform-warning 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='loop-vectorize,loop-unroll,transform-warning' \
+; RUN:   -force-vector-width=4 -force-vector-interleave=1 \
+; RUN:   -enable-epilogue-vectorization -epilogue-vectorization-force-VF=4 \
+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-output=%t.yaml 2>&1
+; RUN: FileCheck --input-file=%t.yaml %s --check-prefix=YAML
+
+; Verify that when the loop vectorizer produces body / epilogue
+; metadata and the unroller *fails* to unroll (runtime unrolling is disabled),
+; the surviving unroll hints reach WarnMissedTransforms, which emits a
+; distinct "not unrolled" warning for each loop-kind qualifier.
+;
+; Pipeline: loop-vectorize -> loop-unroll -> transform-warning.
+; Epilogue vectorization is forced to exercise all four loop categories:
+;
+;   1. plain loop         – not touched by the vectorizer
+;   2. vectorized loop    – main vector body      (has vectorize.body)
+;   3. epilogue loop      – epilogue loop          (has vectorize.epilogue)
+;
+; Runtime unrolling is disabled via metadata so the unroller cannot act,
+; causing the pragma-unroll hint to survive to the warning pass.
+; Both stderr warnings and YAML structured output are checked.
+
+;--- plain_loop: vectorize.enable=false, runtime unroll disabled ---------------
+
+; CHECK:     warning: test.cpp:1:1: loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+; CHECK-NOT: warning: test.cpp:1:1: vectorized
+; CHECK-NOT: warning: test.cpp:1:1: epilogue
+
+define void @plain_loop(ptr noalias %A, i64 %n) !dbg !100 {
+entry:
+  br label %loop, !dbg !108
+loop:
+  %i = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%i.next, %loop]
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i64 %i
+  %v = load i32, ptr %gep, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %v, 1
+  store i32 %add, ptr %gep, align 4
+  %i.next = add nuw nsw i64 %i, 1
+  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %i.next, %n
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit, !dbg !108, !llvm.loop !10
+exit:
+  ret void
+}
+
+;--- vectorizable_loop: vectorized with epilogue, all three fail to unroll -----
+
+; CHECK-DAG: warning: test.cpp:10:1: vectorized loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+; CHECK-DAG: warning: test.cpp:10:1: epilogue loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+
+define void @vectorizable_loop(ptr noalias %A, ptr noalias %B, i64 %n) !dbg !200 {
+entry:
+  br label %loop, !dbg !208
+loop:
+  %i = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%i.next, %loop]
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i64 %i
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i64 %i
+  %v = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %v, 1
+  store i32 %add, ptr %gep.b, align 4
+  %i.next = add nuw nsw i64 %i, 1
+  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %i.next, %n
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit, !dbg !208, !llvm.loop !20
+exit:
+  ret void
+}
+
+;--- YAML checks ---------------------------------------------------------------
+
+; YAML:      --- !Failure
+; YAML:      Pass:            transform-warning
+; YAML:      Name:            FailedRequestedUnrolling
+; YAML:      Function:        plain_loop
+; YAML:      Args:
+; YAML:        - String:          'loop not unrolled:
+
+; YAML:      --- !Failure
+; YAML:      Pass:            transform-warning
+; YAML:      Name:            FailedRequestedUnrolling
+; YAML:      Function:        vectorizable_l

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopTransformWarning/vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopTransformWarning/vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..0168bddacca5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopTransformWarning/vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='loop-vectorize,loop-unroll,transform-warning' \
+; RUN:   -force-vector-width=4 -force-vector-interleave=1 \
+; RUN:   -enable-epilogue-vectorization -epilogue-vectorization-force-VF=4 \
+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-missed=transform-warning 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='loop-vectorize,loop-unroll,transform-warning' \
+; RUN:   -force-vector-width=4 -force-vector-interleave=1 \
+; RUN:   -enable-epilogue-vectorization -epilogue-vectorization-force-VF=4 \
+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-output=%t.yaml 2>&1
+; RUN: FileCheck --input-file=%t.yaml %s --check-prefix=YAML
+
+; Verify that when the loop vectorizer produces body / epilogue
+; metadata and the unroller *fails* to unroll (runtime unrolling is disabled),
+; the surviving unroll hints reach WarnMissedTransforms, which emits a
+; distinct "not unrolled" warning for each loop-kind qualifier.
+;
+; Pipeline: loop-vectorize -> loop-unroll -> transform-warning.
+; Epilogue vectorization is forced to exercise all four loop categories:
+;
+;   1. plain loop         – not touched by the vectorizer
+;   2. vectorized loop    – main vector body      (has vectorize.body)
+;   3. epilogue loop      – epilogue loop          (has vectorize.epilogue)
+;
+; Runtime unrolling is disabled via metadata so the unroller cannot act,
+; causing the pragma-unroll hint to survive to the warning pass.
+; Both stderr warnings and YAML structured output are checked.
+
+;--- plain_loop: vectorize.enable=false, runtime unroll disabled ---------------
+
+; CHECK:     warning: test.cpp:1:1: loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+; CHECK-NOT: warning: test.cpp:1:1: vectorized
+; CHECK-NOT: warning: test.cpp:1:1: epilogue
+
+define void @plain_loop(ptr noalias %A, i64 %n) !dbg !100 {
+entry:
+  br label %loop, !dbg !108
+loop:
+  %i = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%i.next, %loop]
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i64 %i
+  %v = load i32, ptr %gep, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %v, 1
+  store i32 %add, ptr %gep, align 4
+  %i.next = add nuw nsw i64 %i, 1
+  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %i.next, %n
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit, !dbg !108, !llvm.loop !10
+exit:
+  ret void
+}
+
+;--- vectorizable_loop: vectorized with epilogue, all three fail to unroll -----
+
+; CHECK-DAG: warning: test.cpp:10:1: vectorized loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+; CHECK-DAG: warning: test.cpp:10:1: epilogue loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+
+define void @vectorizable_loop(ptr noalias %A, ptr noalias %B, i64 %n) !dbg !200 {
+entry:
+  br label %loop, !dbg !208
+loop:
+  %i = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%i.next, %loop]
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i64 %i
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i64 %i
+  %v = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %v, 1
+  store i32 %add, ptr %gep.b, align 4
+  %i.next = add nuw nsw i64 %i, 1
+  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %i.next, %n
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit, !dbg !208, !llvm.loop !20
+exit:
+  ret void
+}
+
+;--- YAML checks ---------------------------------------------------------------
+
+; YAML:      --- !Failure
+; YAML:      Pass:            transform-warning
+; YAML:      Name:            FailedRequestedUnrolling
+; YAML:      Function:        plain_loop
+; YAML:      Args:
+; YAML:        - String:          'loop not unrolled:
+
+; YAML:      --- !Failure
+; YAML:      Pass:            transform-warning
+; YAML:      Name:            FailedRequestedUnrolling
+; YAML:      Function:        vectorizable_l

Summary: This commit changes GUID handling from repeated AssignGUIDPass::getGUID computations toward GUIDs stored on GlobalValue metadata and accessed through GlobalValue APIs. It adds AssignGUIDPass::runOnModule to assign GUIDs to defined globals and functions, changes GUID consumers in cloning, inlining, call promotion, function import, and JumpTableToSwitch, and introduces a CloneModule CopyMD lambda used on declaration and non-cloned-definition paths.
Changed symbols: AssignGUIDPass::runOnModule; llvm::CloneModule; CopyMD; JumpTableToSwitchPass::run; llvm::InlineFunction; FunctionImportGlobalProcessing::getLinkage; llvm::promoteCallWithIfThenElse
Behavioral change: AssignGUIDPass::runOnModule iterates module globals and functions, skips declarations, and invokes assignGUID on definitions.; GUID consumers switch from AssignGUIDPass::getGUID to GlobalValue GUID accessors, including getGUID, getGUIDIfAssigned, and getGUIDOrFallback.; JumpTableToSwitch now uses an already-assigned GUID when available and otherwise falls back to its existing GUID computation path.; CloneModule's declaration and non-cloned-definition paths invoke a new CopyMD lambda; the lambda body is not included in the retrieved hunk.

+//===-- AssignGUID.cpp - Unique identifier assignment pass ------*- C++ -*-===//
+//
+// Part of the LLVM Project, under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.
+// See https://llvm.org/LICENSE.txt for license information.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+//
+// This file provides a pass which assigns GUID (globally unique identifier)
+// metadata to every GlobalValue in the module, according to its current name,
+// linkage, and originating file. It is idempotent -- if GUID metadata is
+// already present, it does nothing.
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#include "llvm/Transforms/Utils/AssignGUID.h"
+#include "llvm/Support/Debug.h"
+
+using namespace llvm;
+
+void AssignGUIDPass::runOnModule(Module &M) {
+  for (auto &GV : M.globals()) {
+    if (GV.isDeclaration())
+      continue;
+    GV.assignGUID();
+  }
+  for (auto &F : M.functions()) {
+    if (F.isDeclaration())
+      continue;
+    F.assignGUID();
+  }
+}

steps.subject: [LICM][SimplifyCFG] Ignore frees for writable dereferenceability check (#202589)

evidence: Broadens LICM scalar-promotion and SimplifyCFG store-speculation legality by allowing writable checks to ignore intervening frees.
These passes can move or introduce memory operations and maintain memory-analysis state, making this the strongest indirect route to a later MemorySSA clobber/dominance verification failure.
features: dereferenceability-ignore-free, licm-memory-transformation, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/include/llvm/Analysis, path:llvm/lib/Analysis/Loads.cpp, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes dereferenceability checking so selected writable-pointer checks may ignore potential frees. The implementation threads an IgnoreFree parameter through dereferenceability and assumption-based queries, while SimplifyCFG store speculation and LICM scalar-promotion explicitly pass IgnoreFree=true because their comments state that an actual access has already established dereferenceability and the remaining query is only for the writable contract.
Changed symbols: isSafeToSpeculateStore; llvm::promoteLoopAccessesToScalars; llvm::isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer; isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointerViaAssumption
Behavioral change: Dereferenceability analysis can now suppress the willNotFreeBetween check when IgnoreFree is true, including through relocation, bitcast/select recursion, and assumption-based reasoning.; SimplifyCFG may regard a store as safe to speculate when writability is proven while intervening frees are ignored.; LICM scalar promotion may accept a pointer for its writable-contract check despite potential frees, after the pass's preceding access proof.

+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt < %s -mtriple aarch64-- -passes=consthoist -S | FileCheck %s
+
+; The PHI node has some inbound edges with constants that originate from
+; basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry. Those could be tricky
+; to update when trying to find insertion points etc for a common base
+; constant.
+
+; The test case was added as a regression test to show that that we no longer
+; hit assertion failures about number of users updated/rebased. The workaround
+; is to ignore phi edges from basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry
+; when looking for candidate constants.
+
+define i64 @func(i1 %b0, i1 %b1) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @func(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[B0:%.*]], i1 [[B1:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B0]], label %[[BLOCK1:.*]], label %[[BLOCK2:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST1:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK2]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B1]], label %[[BLOCK3:.*]], label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK3]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE1:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE2:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[MERGE]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE1]] ], [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE2]] ], [ [[CONST1]], %[[BLOCK1]] ], [ [[CONST]], %[[BLOCK3]] ], [ 0, %[[BLOCK2]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[V]]
+;
+entry:
+  br i1 %b0, label %block1, label %block2
+
+block1:
+  br label %merge
+
+block2:
+  br i1 %b1, label %block3, label %merge
+
+block3:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable1:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable2:
+  br label %merge
+
+merge:
+  %v = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %unreachable1 ], [ 4886718345, %unreachable2 ], [ 4886718345, %block1 ], [ 4886718345, %block3 ], [ 0, %block2 ]

Summary: This LoopInterchange crash fix changes moveLCSSAPhis to treat followLCSSA results as potentially non-instruction Values. Instead of unconditionally casting the result to Instruction and dereferencing its parent, it uses dyn_cast and skips the PHI when the value is a constant or another non-instruction.
Changed symbols: moveLCSSAPhis; followLCSSA
Behavioral change: LoopInterchange no longer asserts or crashes when followLCSSA returns a non-Instruction value such as a constant.; LCSSA PHIs whose followed incoming value is not an instruction are skipped by the PHI-moving logic.; A regression test adds a loop-interchange case with a constant-rooted LCSSA incoming value.
Assertion or trace link: crash
Reproducer link: The added test reproduces LoopInterchange handling of an LCSSA PHI whose incoming use-def chain reaches a constant.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopInterchange; LCSSA
Causal explanation: The commit fixes a crash in a scalar loop transformation, but the visible failure mode is an invalid cast after followLCSSA returns a constant. It does not touch MemorySSA, MemorySSA.cpp, ClobberWalker, or MemorySSA dominance/update APIs. LCSSA and loop restructuring can generally interact with dominance-sensitive analyses, but the retrieved change only guards a type assumption and has no evidence-backed path to the reported MemorySSA clobber-walker verification assertion.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..2fdee2ae94e9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -mtriple=x86_64 -loop-reduce -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+declare i1 @otherfn(ptr)
+
+; The use of %ptr in %gep outside the loop uses a fixup of 8 which is
+; incompatible with the use inside the loop as an argument to a call. We
+; therefore can't merge the two, as it would cause an assertion failure.
+
+define i64 @invalid_offset_outside_loop(ptr %ptr.arg, i64 %iv.arg) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @invalid_offset_outside_loop(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr [[PTR_ARG:%.*]], i64 [[IV_ARG:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = add i64 [[IV_ARG]], -2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP_INC:.*]] ], [ [[TMP0]], %[[ENTRY]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[PTR_ARG]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[PTR_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP_INC]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CALL:%.*]] = call i1 @otherfn(ptr [[PTR]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CALL]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[LOOP_INC]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP_INC]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR_NEXT]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 16
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV_NEXT]], -3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND]], label %[[EXIT]], label %[[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp slt i64 [[TMP1]], [[IV_ARG]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP2:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL1:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i64 1, i64 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL2:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP2]], i64 [[SEL1]], i64 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SEL2]], ptr [[GEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %ptr = phi ptr [ %ptr.arg, %entry ], [ %ptr.next, %loop.inc ]
+  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.arg, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop.inc ]
+  %call = call i1 @otherfn(ptr %ptr)
+  br i1 %call, label %exit, label %loop.inc
+
+loop.inc:
+  %ptr.next = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 16
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, -1
+  %exitcond = icmp eq i64 %iv, 0
+  br i1 %exitcond, label %exit, label %loop
+
+exit:
+  %cmp1 = icmp slt i64 %iv, %iv.arg
+  %cmp2 = icmp eq i64 %iv, 1
+  %sel1 = select i1 %cmp1, i64 1, i64 2
+  %sel2 = select i1 %cmp2, i64 %sel1, i64 3
+  %gep = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 8
+  store i64 %sel2, ptr %gep, align 8
+  %sub = add i64 %iv, -2
+  ret i64 %sub
+}
+
+; Stream 0 has two in-loop loads at relative offsets {-2^30, 0}, which makes
+; GenerateConstantOffsets produce formulae with BaseOffset +2^30. The exit
+; block loads at +1.5*2^30 past the post-inc pointer; x86 accepts that as a
+; disp32, so the merge gate isLegalUse(LU.MinOffset, LU.MaxOffset, ...,
+; Formulae[0]) passes, but 2^30 + 1.5*2^30 = 2.5*2^30 does not fit in a
+; signed 32-bit displacement, so the +2^30 formulae become illegal once the
+; outside-loop fixup is merged in. The test is sized so that the merge itself
+; drops EstimateSearchSpaceComplexity() below ComplexityLimit, so no later
+; narrowing step deletes the now-illegal formulae before Solve().
+
+define i32 @illegal_formula_after_merge(ptr %p, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @illegal_formula_after_merge(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr [[P:%.*]], i64 [[N:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[P0_LOAD:%.*]] = load ptr, ptr [[P]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ARRAYIDX1:%.*]] = getelementptr ptr, ptr [[P]], i64 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[P1_LOAD:%.*]] = load ptr, pt

top_candidates.subject: [IRBuilder] Refactor for intrinsics const-folding (NFC) (#202738)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Refactors intrinsic creation to accommodate IRBuilder intrinsic constant folding: several callers now accept Value rather than CallInst results, debug locations are set through the builder before creation, and LoopIdiomRecognize's strided-store path explicitly uses CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding where it requires an actual call instruction. Related callers in SimplifyLibCalls and ScalarEvolutionExpander are adjusted to the revised creation interface.
Changed symbols: createPopcntIntrinsic; createFFSIntrinsic; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopStridedStore; LoopIdiomRecognize::recognizeShiftUntilZero; LoopIdiomRecognize::recognizeShiftUntilBitTest; LibCallSimplifier::replacePowWithExp; SCEVExpander::generateOverflowCheck
Behavioral change: Intrinsic construction may now be treated as returning a general Value rather than necessarily a CallInst, allowing constant-folded results at affected call sites.; createPopcntIntrinsic and createFFSIntrinsic set the builder's current debug location before creating the intrinsic instead of setting the location on a returned CallInst.; LoopIdiomRecognize's strided-store transformation switches to CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding, preserving production of a call where that path requires one.; The exp10 replacement transfers IR flags through the CreateIntrinsic callback rather than requiring a separately named CallInst.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSAAnalysis preservation is visible in the LoopIdiomRecognize pass context.
Reproducer link: No retrieved test or hunk ties intrinsic constant folding, loop idiom recognition, or the changed call/result types to the reported -O1 MemorySSA clobber-walker assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: IRBuilder intrinsic construction; LoopIdiomRecognize; ScalarEvolutionExpander; MemorySSAAnalysis preservation
Causal explanation: The strongest available connection is that LoopIdiomRecognize is constructed with AR.MSSA and preserves MemorySSAAnalysis when it changes a loop. A change that causes intrinsic creation to fold away an instruction could affect transformation shape or analysis-preservation assumptions. But the patch explicitly uses CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding in the visible strided-store path requiring a call, is labeled NFC, and contains no direct MemorySSA, ClobberWalker, dominance, updater, or verifier change. The evidence for this commit causing the specific assertion is weak.
Causal confidence: 0.16
Build risk: Several CallInst variables and helper return types are widened to Value, so compile-time type checking covers many incorrect assumptions.; The strided-store path deliberately opts out of folding, signaling that call-versus-value identity matters for that transformation.; No regression-test additions are visible in the retrieved hunks.; Debug-location handling changes from post-creation assignment to builder state, which can affect metadata attachment behavior even though the stated change is NFC.

top_candidates.subject: [ConstantHoisting] Skip PHI edges from unreachable blocks (#203892)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes ConstantHoisting candidate collection to ignore constants used through PHI incoming edges from blocks unreachable from function entry. This avoids attempting to analyze, choose insertion points for, or rebase candidate uses associated with unreachable predecessor edges, fixing prior constant-hoisting assertion failures on such CFGs.
Changed symbols: ConstantHoistingPass::collectConstantCandidates
Behavioral change: When examining a PHINode use, obtains the corresponding incoming basic block.; Skips that PHI incoming edge if DominatorTree::isReachableFromEntry reports the predecessor is unreachable.; Prevents unreachable PHI-edge constants from entering constant-hoisting candidate analysis and rebasing.; Converts an existing expected-crash regression into a normal passing test and adds a focused unreachable-PHI-edge regression test.
Assertion or trace link: The commit addresses assertion failures, but its tests describe a ConstantHoisting assertion about the number of users updated or rebased.; The retrieved patch does not contain MemorySSA, ClobberWalker, verifyOptResult, OtherClobbers, or MSSA.dominates.
Reproducer link: The new reproducer has unreachable basic blocks feeding PHI nodes and verifies ConstantHoisting does not crash.; This differs from the reported reduced C testcase whose failure is in MemorySSA clobber-walker verification at -O1.
Pass or subsystem link: ConstantHoisting; DominatorTree reachability
Causal explanation: The change is relevant to optimizer CFG and dominance correctness: it explicitly avoids treating unreachable PHI predecessors as normal candidate-use paths. Such malformed-or-unreachable CFG handling can indirectly affect later analyses, but the hunk changes only ConstantHoisting candidate filtering and has no visible MemorySSA mutation or verification interaction. The evidence supports a weak indirect risk, not a direct causal match.
Causal confidence: 0.12
Build risk: The change is a localized early continue guarded by an existing DominatorTree reachability API.; Regression tests cover an unreachable-PHI-edge assertion case and update a previously expected-crash ConstantHoisting test to require successful execution.; The behavior intentionally reduces optimization opportunities for constants appearing only on unreachable PHI incoming edges.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/ConstantHoisting/AArch64/consthoist-unreachable-phi-edge.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/ConstantHoisting/AArch64/consthoist-unreachable-phi-edge.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..65bce13bf022
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/ConstantHoisting/AArch64/consthoist-unreachable-phi-edge.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt < %s -mtriple aarch64-- -passes=consthoist -S | FileCheck %s
+
+; The PHI node has some inbound edges with constants that originate from
+; basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry. Those could be tricky
+; to update when trying to find insertion points etc for a common base
+; constant.
+
+; The test case was added as a regression test to show that that we no longer
+; hit assertion failures about number of users updated/rebased. The workaround
+; is to ignore phi edges from basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry
+; when looking for candidate constants.
+
+define i64 @func(i1 %b0, i1 %b1) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @func(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[B0:%.*]], i1 [[B1:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B0]], label %[[BLOCK1:.*]], label %[[BLOCK2:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST1:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK2]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B1]], label %[[BLOCK3:.*]], label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK3]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE1:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE2:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[MERGE]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE1]] ], [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE2]] ], [ [[CONST1]], %[[BLOCK1]] ], [ [[CONST]], %[[BLOCK3]] ], [ 0, %[[BLOCK2]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[V]]
+;
+entry:
+  br i1 %b0, label %block1, label %block2
+
+block1:
+  br label %merge
+
+block2:
+  br i1 %b1, label %block3, label %merge
+
+block3:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable1:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable2:
+  br label %merge
+
+merge:
+  %v = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %unreachable1 ], [ 4886718345, %unreachable2 ], [ 4886718345, %block1 ], [ 4886718345, %block3 ], [ 0, %block2 ]
+  ret i64 %v
+}
+
+

causal_evidence.summary: This SimpleLoopUnswitch change generalizes trivial unswitching to invariant branches that target a loop latch rather than directly exiting the loop. When the loop has a unique latch exit, the latch is side-effect-free, exit PHIs are loop-invariant, and ScalarEvolution can prove a finite bound, unswitchTrivialBranch rewires the branch's latch edge directly to the unique latch exit, repairs exit PHIs, and applies the corresponding CFG updates through MemorySSAUpdater when available.
behavioral_change: Trivial unswitching now handles an invariant branch with one successor equal to the loop latch and the other remaining in the loop.
The transformation deletes the branch-parent-to-latch CFG edge and inserts a branch-parent-to-unique-latch-exit edge.
The unique latch exit's PHIs receive incoming values for the newly added predecessor, copied from the latch incoming values.
The CFG edge updates are applied through MSSAU->applyUpdates(Updates, DT) when MemorySSAUpdater is present, otherwise through DominatorTree::applyUpdates.
The pre-existing loop-exit-PHI check is bypassed after this new rewrite has already modified the branch.

reproducer: The new trivial-unswitch regression test runs simple-loop-unswitch under loop-mssa and exercises exactly the new latch-bypass CFG rewrite.
The visible phase-ordering test updates O1 expected CFG shape after the generalized unswitching transformation.
The transformation changes predecessor relationships and exit PHIs while incrementally updating MemorySSA, which is the class of state that can affect clobber-walker dominance verification.
issue_link.explanation: This is the strongest candidate in the retrieved evidence. It introduces a new CFG rewrite in a loop-mssa pass and directly invokes MSSAU->applyUpdates for a paired edge deletion/insertion after changing predecessor and PHI structure. The issue's OtherClobbers/MSSA.dominates/ClobberWalker verification signal is specifically consistent with an incremental MemorySSA or dominance-state mismatch after CFG updates. The hunks do not prove that this rewrite produces the reported testcase failure, but they provide a direct mechanism and O1-relevant coverage.

build_risk: The new path combines CFG rewiring, PHI repair, DominatorTree updates, and MemorySSAUpdater updates, making invariant-maintenance regressions plausible.
A new large loop-mssa regression test explicitly exercises the latch-bypass transformation.
Visible O1 phase-ordering test expectations change, indicating pipeline-observable behavior at O1.
The retrieval reports 59 omitted hunks, so related implementation or test changes outside the shown evidence remain uninspected.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

Summary: This NFC-labelled GVN change alters where AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue inserts a rematerialized select: it now uses the caller-provided insertion point rather than the original select's iterator. The accompanying GVN checks update expected select ordering and debug locations, consistent with an instruction-placement-only change.
Changed symbols: AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue; GVN
Behavioral change: A rematerialized SelectInst is inserted before InsertPt rather than before the original SelectInst.; GVN/PRE-generated select ordering and associated debug-location ordering can change.
Reproducer link: The change affects GVN load/select PRE materialization, but the retrieved hunks contain no MemorySSA verifier, clobber-walker, dominance, or MemorySSA-update logic.
Pass or subsystem link: GVN; Scalar optimizer
Causal explanation: The issue concerns a MemorySSA clobber-walker verification failure. This commit operates in a scalar optimization that materializes values derived from loads, so it is loosely adjacent to memory-dependence optimization. However, the changed instruction is a select, which has no memory access, and the visible change neither constructs nor updates MemorySSA. The NFC subject and test-only ordering/debug-location adjustments further weaken a direct causal link.
Causal confidence: 0.10

top_candidates.subject: [IRBuilder] Refactor for intrinsics const-folding (NFC) (#202738)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This NFC IRBuilder refactor adapts scalar and utility callers to intrinsic creation that can yield a Value rather than necessarily a CallInst, consistent with intrinsic constant folding. LoopIdiomRecognize changes several CallInst-typed intrinsic results to Value, moves debug-location assignment to the builder before intrinsic creation, and uses CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding for a strided-store transformation that requires an instruction result. SimplifyLibCalls moves flag copying into the CreateIntrinsic callback, while ScalarEvolutionExpander similarly changes an overflow-intrinsic result variable to Value.
Changed symbols: LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopStridedStore; createPopcntIntrinsic; createFFSIntrinsic; LoopIdiomRecognize::recognizeShiftUntilZero; LoopIdiomRecognize::recognizeShiftUntilBitTest; LibCallSimplifier::replacePowWithExp; SCEVExpander::generateOverflowCheck; IRBuilder::CreateIntrinsic
Behavioral change: Intrinsic construction at the edited call sites may now be represented as a generic Value rather than assumed to be a newly created CallInst, accommodating constant folding.; LoopIdiomRecognize explicitly disables folding for the strided-store intrinsic creation site where an instruction result is required.; Debug locations for the popcount and find-first-set helpers are set on the IRBuilder before intrinsic construction rather than assigned afterward to a returned CallInst.; The exp10 replacement copies IR flags through the intrinsic-creation callback rather than after receiving a CallInst.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSAAnalysis appears in the retrieved LoopIdiomRecognize pass context, but no MemorySSA assertion, ClobberWalker, OtherClobbers, MSSA.dominates, or verifyOptResult term is changed in the hunks.
Reproducer link: The shown changes can alter whether an intrinsic is materialized as an instruction, but no reduced -O1 crashing testcase or MemorySSA verifier test is included.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopIdiomRecognize; SimplifyLibCalls; ScalarEvolutionExpander; MemorySSAAnalysis (context only)
Causal explanation: LoopIdiomRecognize is a potentially relevant scalar optimization because the retrieved function context shows it receives AR.MSSA and preserves MemorySSAAnalysis after successful transformations. An unexpected fold that removes or changes an instruction could indirectly affect MemorySSA's view of transformed IR. However, the displayed edits do not modify MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater usage, dominance maintenance, memory accesses, or clobber-walker verification; the one visibly instruction-sensitive LoopIdiomRecognize site is changed to CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding. The evidence therefore supports only a weak indirect connection.

top_candidates.subject: [InstCombine] Fold X == Identity ? Y : min/max(X, Y) (#202748)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends InstructionSimplify's operand-replacement simplification for min/max intrinsics. In simplifyWithOpsReplaced, when one replacement operand equals a MinMaxIntrinsic identity value, the intrinsic is replaced with its other operand; poison-generating annotations are preserved conservatively by requiring flag dropping and recording the intrinsic in DropFlags. The accompanying InstCombine tests cover signed and unsigned min/max select patterns and a range-annotation case.
Changed symbols: simplifyWithOpsReplaced; MinMaxIntrinsic; InstructionSimplify
Behavioral change: Folds a min/max intrinsic to its non-identity operand after operand replacement when the other operand is the intrinsic identity.; Rejects the fold when poison-generating annotations exist and flags cannot be dropped; otherwise records the intrinsic for flag removal.; Enables InstCombine test cases such as select of a min/max result guarded by comparison against the corresponding min/max identity.
Pass or subsystem link: InstructionSimplify; InstCombine
Causal explanation: The shown change affects value-level simplification of arithmetic min/max intrinsics and has no displayed MemorySSA, clobber-walker, dominance, memory-access, or MemorySSA-update logic. It could only be related indirectly if the altered scalar IR exposed a separate MemorySSA defect, but the retrieved evidence provides no direct path to the reported OtherClobbers/MSSA.dominates verification assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.05
Build risk: Implementation change is covered by newly added InstCombine regression tests for umin, umax, smin, and smax patterns.; The fold explicitly handles poison-generating annotations through DropFlags, reducing semantic-regression risk.; No build-system, MemorySSA, or verifier test changes are shown.

evidence: Introduces a new SimpleLoopUnswitch CFG-rewrite path that explicitly updates MemorySSA through MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The SimpleLoopUnswitch change generalizes trivial unswitching to handle a loop-invariant branch whose one in-loop successor is the loop latch and whose other successor remains in the loop. When the loop has a unique latch exit, invariant exit PHIs, no side effects in the latch, and a computable finite backedge count, unswitchTrivialBranch rewrites the branch-to-latch edge into a branch-to-latch-exit edge, updates exit PHIs, and applies corresponding CFG updates through either MSSAU or DominatorTree before continuing ordinary trivial-unswitch processing.
Changed symbols: unswitchTrivialBranch; SimpleLoopUnswitch; MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates; DominatorTree::applyUpdates; areLoopExitPHIsLoopInvariant; Loop::getLoopLatch; Loop::getUniqueLatchExitBlock
Behavioral change: Permits trivial unswitching of an invariant guard that previously could only be recognized when it directly branched to a loop exit.; Replaces a CFG edge from the branch parent to the loop latch with an edge to the unique latch-exit block, removes the predecessor from the latch, and adds equivalent incoming values to latch-exit PHIs.; Updates MemorySSA through MSSAU->applyUpdates when an updater is available; otherwise updates the DominatorTree directly.; Restricts the new latch-bypass rewrite to finite loops with side-effect-free latches and loop-invariant exit PHIs.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll

index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

@@ -309,0 +310,24 @@ gpu.module @test_kernel [#xevm.target<chip = "pvc">] {
+  // f8E8M0FNU has no native LLVM representation. The load must use the integer
+  // storage type from the XeVM type converter (i8) and then materialize back
+  // to f8E8M0FNU, rather than emitting an illegal llvm.load of f8E8M0FNU.
+  //CHECK-LABEL: load_matrix_f8e8m0_scalar
+  gpu.func @load_matrix_f8e8m0_scalar(%arg0: memref<1024xi8, 3>) -> vector<1x1xf8E8M0FNU> {
+    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
+    %0 = xegpu.create_mem_desc %arg0 : memref<1024xi8, 3> -> !xegpu.mem_desc<32x32xf8E8M0FNU>
+    %tid_x = gpu.thread_id x
+    //CHECK: %[[LOADED:.*]] = llvm.load %{{.*}} : !llvm.ptr<3> -> i8
+    //CHECK: %[[BCAST:.*]] = arith.bitcast %[[LOADED]] : i8 to f8E8M0FNU
+    //CHECK: vector.broadcast %[[BCAST]] : f8E8M0FNU to vector<1x1xf8E8M0FNU>
+    %1 = xegpu.load_matrix %0[%c0, %tid_x]: !xegpu.mem_desc<32x32xf8E8M0FNU>, index, index -> vector<1x1xf8E8M0FNU>
+    gpu.return %1 : vector<1x1xf8E8M0FNU>
+  }
+
+  //CHECK-LABEL: load_matrix_f8e8m0_vector
+  gpu.func @load_matrix_f8e8m0_vector(%arg0: memref<1024xi8, 3>) -> vector<8xf8E8M0FNU> {
+    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
+    %0 = xegpu.create_mem_desc %arg0 : memref<1024xi8, 3> -> !xegpu.mem_desc<32x32xf8E8M0FNU>
+    //CHECK: %[[LOADEDV:.*]] = llvm.load %{{.*}} : !llvm.ptr<3> -> vector<8xi8>
+    //CHECK: vector.bitcast %[[LOADEDV]] : vector<8xi8> to vector<8xf8E8M0FNU>
+    %1 = xegpu.load_matrix %0[%c0, %c0]: !xegpu.mem_desc<32x32xf8E8M0FNU>, index, index -> vector<8xf8E8M0FNU>
+    gpu.return %1 : vector<8xf8E8M0FNU>
+  }

+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,
